retired: a deprecated alias, deleted after its one release; the row records the rename
why: stop a spinning executor WITHOUT finalizing it -- flips `rclc_executor_state_t` back from SPINNING to INITIALIZED so `rclc_executor_spin`'s loop exits and the session stays open for a later spin. rclc's `rclc_executor_spin` has no way out at all. The scenario is a mode change on an RTOS task (safe-state, OTA staging) where tearing the middleware down and re-opening it costs a full discovery round. OUR LANGUAGES USED TO DISAGREE, three ways, with C++ missing the capability entirely: C `nros_executor_stop`, Rust `Executor::halt` / `is_halted` / `halt_flag`, rclcpp `Executor::cancel`, and a C++ `spin()` that exited only on `shutdown()` -- which calls `nros_cpp_fini` and destroys the session. phase-417 W4.c settled it on rclcpp's spelling in all three: `rclc_executor_cancel` / `rclc_executor_is_spinning` (C), `Executor::cancel` / `is_spinning` (C++ and Rust). This name is what is left of the old C spelling -- a deprecated `static inline` forwarder. phase-417 W4.c CORRECTION (2026-09-13) — this row said C exports no `is_spinning` reader and that the three languages carry the capability under three spellings. Both went stale the moment W4.c landed and nothing re-read them: `rclc_executor_cancel` and `rclc_executor_is_spinning` are exported C entry points (`packages/api/nros-c/src/executor.rs`, declared in `nros_generated.h`), and `nros_executor_stop` survives only as a deprecated `static inline` forwarder onto the new name. So the three languages now agree on ONE spelling — rclcpp's — rather than on three. CORRECTED 2026-10-27 (phase-515 W0.b): the `nros_executor_stop` forwarder has since been removed; `rclc_executor_cancel` is the only C spelling.
